title: vibeX docs — the authoring contract
description: What a person or agent WRITES. It holds only what cannot be computed: prose tied to code, and statements a human stands behind. Facts that can be derived from a diagram spec are never authored here — a section asks for a generator and the build derives them. See docs-graph.schema.json for what the build EMITS.

covers.description: Spec ids this document documents, e.g. ["shop.c4", "orders.erd"]. Generators may only read specs listed here, so the coverage report can state exactly what was and was not looked at.

review_window_days.description: How long an asserted claim stays trusted before the build downgrades it to `expired`. Shorter for fast-moving areas.

sections.description: Reading order for humans. Agents read the flat claim list instead, so section order carries no meaning for them.

summary.description: One sentence on what the section answers. Not a claim: never rendered as fact, never cited.

claims.description: Ids of authored claims to render here, in this order.

generate.description: Derived content to compute into this section. A fixed set: the agent chooses WHICH facts appear, never what they say.

narrative.description: Markdown prose for this section, so the document reads as a document. Cite a claim with [[claim-id]]: the citation resolves to that claim and carries its confidence, and the build fails if it does not resolve. Prose is not evidence — every load-bearing statement in it should carry a citation, and the claims it cites render below it as the section's evidence. Supported: headings, paragraphs, lists, blockquotes, fenced code, tables, horizontal rules, and inline bold/italic/code/link. Raw HTML is escaped, never rendered.

claims.description: One claim = one assertion. If a sentence contains an `and` joining two independent facts, it is two claims. This is what makes a claim individually citable, individually checkable, and individually retractable.

glossary.description: Domain words whose meaning is not guessable from the code. Agents use this to map user wording onto spec ids.

definition.description: Plain English, no jargon that is not itself in the glossary.

see.description: The thing in a diagram this word names.

coverage.description: The document's own boundary, stated up front. A doc that admits what it does not cover is trusted where it does.

reason.description: Why it is absent and where to look instead. "Not documented yet" is a valid reason; silence is not.

ref.description: Address of a thing in another spec: `<spec-id>` or `<spec-id>#<node-id>`, e.g. `shop.c4#bff`, `orders.erd#orders`. Same shape as the viewer's deep links, so a ref pastes straight into a URL.

claim.description: A single checkable statement. Note there is no `confidence` field: you declare your evidence, the build computes how far it can be trusted. Declaring your own confidence is how documentation starts lying.

id.description: Stable and addressable. Agents cite this id; changing it breaks those citations, so supersede instead of rename.

text.description: One sentence of plain English, present tense, stating what IS. No hedging ("probably", "should"), no history ("we used to"), no instructions ("you should") — those are not claims about the system.

subject.description: What the claim is about. Puts the claim on that node's page in the docs, and answers an agent asking "what do you know about X".

supersedes.description: Id of a claim this replaces. The old claim stays in the graph marked superseded, so a stale citation resolves to a tombstone rather than nothing.

source.description: Where the claim's authority comes from. Only two kinds may be authored; `derived` is emitted by the build and is invalid here.

anchored.description: Prose about code, pinned to the code it describes. When that code changes the claim is flagged for re-reading — it is not silently assumed still true, and not silently assumed false either.

path.description: Repo-relative POSIX path: no leading slash, drive letter, URL scheme, or ".." segment.

symbol.description: Class, function, or export the claim is about. Used in the source link and in the failure message when the anchor breaks.

hash.description: First 12 hex chars of the SHA-256 of the anchored region: the selected lines (whole file when line is absent), normalised per hash_mode and joined with \n. loose: each line's whitespace runs collapsed to one space and trimmed, so a reformat does not cry wolf. exact: leading indentation kept, only trailing whitespace, line endings and trailing blank lines ignored, so re-nesting a line in Python or YAML is caught.

hash_mode.description: Overrides the per-extension default. Loose only for known whitespace-insensitive languages (TypeScript, JavaScript, JSON, Java, Go, Rust, C-family, SQL, GraphQL, Prisma, CSS...); everything else, including every unknown extension, is exact. vibex validate warns when loose is set on a file where indentation is syntax.

asserted.description: Something a person decided, which no file can prove: ownership, rationale, a deliberate trade-off. Always rendered as someone's statement, never as a system fact.

by.description: Who stands behind it. A person or team, not "the docs" and not a model name.

at.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) this was last confirmed true — not when it was first written. Re-confirming is an edit to this field.

rationale.description: Why, when the why is the point. Kept separate from `text` so the claim stays one sentence.
